label: Inference
claim: The shared filter classifies a row as an aggregate only when its parsed dot-segment position has at least one direct child in the same context; it removes only those parent row IDs, preserves all other source order, and emits integrity warnings rather than restoring parents.

hypothesis_matrix.leaf_only_prevents_double_count: included: parent rows are excluded before downstream aggregation
hypothesis_matrix.direct_child_sum_validates_aggregates: included: compares a parent only with parsed immediate children at Decimal 0.01 tolerance

details.limitations: A syntactically valid position hierarchy can still encode a business structure that the source author did not intend as additive.

label: Inference
claim: The drawing-card workflow applies hierarchy filtering immediately after extraction and before matcher calls, manual review, and aggregate_rows; its context is file ID plus sheet. Training-data preparation applies the same filter before detail/outdated/duplicate processing, with a finer document/object context. Thus leaf filtering is call-site compatible and a later matcher or unit-mismatch review has no code path that re-adds an excluded parent.

compatibility.drawing_card: filter -> reject parent -> matcher -> aggregate -> review
compatibility.resource_detail: no resource/detail classifier is consulted by either hierarchy filter

details.risk: The drawing-card context is less granular than training-data context; repeated numbering inside one file/sheet but across unrepresented subobjects could create false parent-child relations.

label: Inference
claim: The supplied private run processed 4 uploaded workbooks, selected 3 current-period schemas, extracted 48,129 rows, excluded 5,139 hierarchy parents before classification, then made 42,990 classification decisions. The arithmetic relationship exactly accounts for the parent exclusions, demonstrating that the filter is active on the production-shaped sample rather than only in unit tests.

details.limitations: One supplied workbook was not selected because it is another period; this is evidence about the run selection, not its workbook contents.

label: Inference
claim: The proposed standalone-work rule 'unit plus quantity proves standalone work' is falsified in the supplied run: 1,167 of 13,699 rows that have a non-empty work name, unit, quantity, and cost were nevertheless hierarchy parents. Keeping all rows with those fields would therefore reintroduce at least 1,167 known aggregate rows (8.5% of that heuristic-positive set). Even requiring a positive quantity leaves 713 known parents.

details.false_positive_risk: High: field completeness is not a hierarchy discriminator.
details.false_negative_risk: Unknown: no manually labelled standalone parent population is available.

label: Inference
claim: Direct-child sum checks are useful only as integrity gates, not as the predicate for selecting a parent: the supplied run recorded 3,958 direct-child cost mismatches, 35 missing-direct-child costs, 92 duplicate positions, and 21 position gaps, while still excluding the detected parents. Selecting by a matching sum would retain aggregates with incomplete or non-additive child values and make duplicate prevention contingent on financial data.

details.method: read-only issue-code count plus static inspection

contradiction_matrix.proposed_rule: exclude parent only when direct-child total equals parent amount
contradiction_matrix.support: a matched total supports an additive parent interpretation
contradiction_matrix.disconfirmation: 3993 parent rows emitted mismatch or missing-cost issues; equality is absent/unsafe for many detected parents
contradiction_matrix.decision: reject as selection predicate; retain as warning/blocker for contributing descendants

contradiction_matrix.disconfirmation: duplicate positions and coarse drawing-card context can create structural false positives
contradiction_matrix.decision: accept only with unambiguous detected position column and scoped context; otherwise fail closed/manual review

details.financial_confirmation: No automatic financial confirmation is recommended; the existing check is an integrity warning and strict-publication blocker only when affected descendants contribute.

label: Inference
claim: Focused regression coverage passed 22 tests covering exact segment boundaries, nested parents, suffix siblings, direct-child-only sums, duplicate/missing/gap warnings, drawing-card extraction, training-data exclusion, and strict publication blocking. These tests support a conservative hierarchy rule but do not establish semantic labels for resource-detail rows.

details.method: uv run pytest -q focused hierarchy suite
acceptance_criteria: Parse only exact dot-separated numeric-plus-optional-letter segments; 6.1 must not parent 6.10 and 1 must not parent 1а.
Exclude a row from matching/training only when an unambiguous direct child exists in the same documented context; preserve every non-parent row in source order.
Do not use unit, quantity, work name, or cost presence to override a detected parent.
Compute direct-child sums only for warnings/blockers; never make financial equality a selection condition and never auto-confirm a financial conclusion.
For duplicate position, weak/tied position-column detection, or a context known to merge distinct numbering trees, fail closed to review rather than silently exclude.
Prove with tests that excluded parent IDs cannot enter matcher, manual-review, aggregation, or training output.
details.gap: No labelled sample separates resource-detail rows from standalone work; a semantic exception would need product-owned labels and a new decision.
